result:
All green. Summary of the work:

I implemented the `lifecycle-uc4-uc5` module's 19 endpoints across both AI Clause Analysis (UC4) and Negotiation & Routing (UC5):

- **Models/migrations**: the 10 contract tables were already scaffolded on disk from an interrupted prior run; I verified they match `context.json` exactly (persistence tests enforce this).
- **New code**: schemas, repositories, services and routers for both clause-analysis and negotiation, wired into `app/main.py`.
- **Business rules covered**: overall risk rollup (BR-1), mandatory-clause Missing detection seeded from the UC123 clause library, accept/edit/reject transitions with full audit logging, optimistic-concurrency on edit (AF-004), metadata AI-suggested→User-confirmed relabelling (BR-7), Ask AI validation+disclaimer (AF-005/BR-8), Proceed-to-Negotiation gating (BR-5/AF-006), routing precondition + reviewer validation, Finance Head/Legal Reviewer auto-add, sequential/parallel review submission, With Internal ⇄ With Counterparty ⇄ Agreed transitions, auto-versioning, OTP-secured external party flow with 3-strike lockout, Compare Versions, manual reminders, and comments.
- **Tests**: 35 new tests (167 total, all passing), plus a live server boot confirming all 19 routes in `/openapi.json` with correct methods and that 401/403 role enforcement works end-to-end.
- **Blockers recorded** (10 items) for things this sandbox genuinely can't do correctly: no real AI/document-parsing pipeline (clause extraction is simulated from the mandatory clause library only), no email service (OTP is returned in the response instead), no scheduler (automatic daily reminders unimplemented), no clause-library-update trigger (BR-16 re-flagging unimplemented), and a direct ownership conflict with another task file (`T-LIFECYCLE-NEGOTIATION-API`) claiming the same two external-party endpoints with a different `auth_required` value.

Output written to `.api-gen/outputs/T-LIFECYCLE-CONTRACTS-API.json` with `status: PARTIAL` given those recorded blockers.
